column1: # dcload-ip-rs: which PPF patch belongs to which dump.
# A mapping list, and it has to be one: what these patches fix is different in
# every title, so unlike the GAPS probe and the cable check there is no content
# signature to look for. See src/patchdb.rs.
# THE LIST IS A CLAIM, THE PATCH CHECKS IT. A PPF3.0 carries 1024 bytes of the
# original file, and a row that names the right patch for the wrong dump is
# refused with a reason rather than applied. A patch with no blockcheck (PPF1.0,
# or PPF3.0 written without one) can prove nothing, and for those the bin_md5
# column is the only thing between the patch and the wrong image -- fill it in.
# Tab-separated. `-` means "no key of this kind"; a row needs at least one.
#   disc_md5   MD5 of the boot sector (IP.BIN sector 0). The identity the rest
#              of this host uses -- `dcload-ip-rs identify <image>` prints it as
#              `boot md5`. Names a dump, not a game.
#   bin_md5    MD5 of the UNPATCHED boot binary, printed as `bin md5`. Narrower,
#              and the one that matters when the patch has no blockcheck.
#   file       the .ppf, in this directory.
#   apply      auto   = applied by itself; --no-ppf turns it off.
#              manual = shipped and reported, applied only with --ppf.
#              Use manual when the patch changes what the title DOES rather
#              than only what it supports.
#   title      what the row is about. Documentation, never a key: the same game
#              is renamed between regions and the same name covers dumps that
#              differ.
#   note       one line, logged when the patch is applied.
# disc_md5
1aae36b0c58051ed3f9c3190a2927dbd
column6: Adds the VGA video path the PAL release was built without, and forces 60 Hz. By japanese_cake, 2015 (jc-snows-60hz-vga.nfo). Pair it with --vga so the cable check and IP.BIN agree; --no-ppf leaves the title as shipped.
